children.game_version: A playful processional game mimicking devil characters with safe foam tridents and simple marching rhythms.

seniors.seated_version: Seated rhythmic tapping using feet and hands to simulate zapateo and cajita patterns.
seniors.standing_version: Supported standing balance march without acrobatic leaps or sudden lunges.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduced tempo and minimized spatial range

movement_profile.formation_and_space: Street procession (comparsa) led by a caporal
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Dynamic and agile movement to accommodate acrobatics
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Includes acrobatic movements and low-to-high level shifts
movement_profile.partnering: Group ensemble interaction rather than couples partnering
movement_profile.posture: Upright and theatrical, adapted for parading and sudden lunges

signature_moves.description: Theatrical movement using a trident to startle onlookers
signature_moves.name: Devil lunge

music_profile.sound_description: A lively street sound driven by strummed guitars, the crisp percussion of the wooden cajita, and the sharp, raspy rattle of the horse or donkey jawbone (quijada).

basic_steps: Comparsa marching formation step led by the caporal
teaching.formation: Comparsa (street procession) led by a caporal
teaching.level_notes: Requires physical stamina for zapateo and acrobatic elements.
